(5)     A package or container of food may bear a Quick Response (QR) code or any other machine-readable code 
solely to provide additional information, and such code shall not be used as a substitute for and shall not conflict

under regulation 3(4) of these regulations, if the supplementary label contains information  in respect of date 
of manufacture, date of packing, date of expiry and other mandatory information, such supplementary label shall 
be affixed securely in a manner that it does not distort, deface or obliterate the original date of manufacture, date of 
packing, date of expiry and other information required to be declared by the manufacturer or packer: 
 
Provided further that, where an imported package or container of food bears the date of manufacture and/ or the 
date of packing and/ or the date of expiry only in coded form, including where such date is encoded within a 
batch number, a code number or a decipherable code marking (including a Julian code/ QR code) printed, 
painted or displayed by the manufacturer or packer, the importer shall, for the purpose of compliance with these 
regulations, affix a supplementary label declaring the corresponding date(s) in the manner and format specified

with any declaration required to be made on the label under regulation 4; further, such code shall be printed, 
painted or affixed in a manner that does not distort, deface, erase or obliterate any information on the original 
label, and any information made available through such code shall not be false, misleading, deceptive or shall 
not be in violation of any provision of these regulations.   
 
4. 
(1)    The following declarations shall be made indelibly and legibly on the main panel- 
(a) 
common name of the product in bold type in all three languages or, in any two of the three languages 
on the main panel and other language on any panel;  
Provided that the common name may be substituted by any other name as set out in Schedule I 
hereto; 
(b) 
trade name and brand name (if any) in any one or more of the three languages in a manner that shall 
not be deceptive or mislead any person; and 
(c) 
the net contents of the package or container expressed in SI units or by the international symbols 
‘g’ or ‘kg’ in the case of solids, ‘ml’ or ‘l’ in the case of liquids and, if packaged in liquid medium, 
the net drained weight expressed as ‘g’ or ‘kg’: 
 
(2) 
(a) 
The following declarations shall be made indelibly and legibly on any panel in any one or more of the 
three languages – 
 
(i) 
a complete list of ingredients used in the food by their common names in descending order 
of ingoing weight (m/m) at the time of manufacture of the food including any permitted food 
additive by its common name and INS number as prescribed by regulations made under the 
Act. However, processing aids that are not carried over to foods are exempted from 
declaration in the list of ingredients;  
 
        Provided that, such exemption shall not apply to the following items: - 
(A) Cereals containing gluten; i.e., wheat, spelt, rye, barley, oats, or their 
hybridised strains and products of these; 
(B) Crustacea and products of these; 
(C) Eggs and egg products; 
(D) Fish and fish products; 
(E) Peanuts, soybeans and products of these; 
(F) Milk and milk products; (lactose included); and 
(G) Tree nuts and nut products. 
 
(ii)    (A)  the name and address of the manufacturer and distributor, and in the case of imported 
food products, in addition the name and address of the importer;  
 
                  (B) the name and address of the packer, if any; 
 
(iii)   the batch number or code number or a decipherable code marking; 
 
(iv)    the date of manufacture;

2.1 Where nutrient declaration is applied as per section 1 above, the declaration of the following 
shall be mandatory: 
 
2.1.1 Energy value;    
2.1.2 The amounts of protein, total sugars (with naturally occurring and added sugar), 
available carbohydrate (i.e. dietary carbohydrate excluding dietary fibre), dietary 
fibre, total fat, saturated fat, trans- fats and sodium; and 
2.1.3 The amount of any other nutrient for which a nutrition claim and/or health claim 
and/or reference is   made on the label. 
 
2.2 Where a claim is made regarding the amount and/or type of fatty acids or the amount of 
cholesterol, the amounts of saturated fatty acids, monounsaturated fatty acids and 
polyunsaturated fatty acids and cholesterol shall be declared, and the amount of trans- fatty

acid is required, in addition to the requirements of section 2.1 and in accordance with section 
4.6. 
 
2.3 In addition to the mandatory declaration under 2.1 and 2.2, vitamins and minerals may be 
listed in accordance with the following criteria: 
 
2.3.1 Only vitamins and minerals for which recommended intakes have been established 
shall be declared; and  
 
2.3.2 When nutrient declaration is applied, vitamins and minerals which are present in 
amounts less than five per centum (5%) of the Nutrient Reference Value (NRV) as 
specified in Schedule IV hereto or the Average Requirement (AR) or Adequate Intake (AI) 
values as specified in Schedule VIII hereto, per one hundred grams (100 g) or one hundred 
milliliters (100 ml) or per serving as quantified on the label shall not be declared.

obligation.text: Business-to-business food products must display 10 mandatory disclosures (common name in either of the three languages, trade name if applicable, net contents, date of manufacture, date of expiry, batch number, manufacturer's name and address, distributor's name and address, country of origin in case of imported foods, complete list of ingredients) and must display 'Not for retail sale' printed on label or affixed through supplementary label in bold type with font size not less than 3 mm.
